problems.title: Integers between two powers
problems.question: How many natural numbers lie strictly between $999^{1/3}$ and $10^{3/2}$?
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
steps: Since 10^(3/2)=√1000, the permitted integers are 10 through 31. Count 31−10+1.

problems.title: Disjoint event probabilities
problems.question: A, B are disjoint, P(A)=.3, P(B complement)=.6. Find P(A∪B).
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: $P(B)=1-.6=.4$. Disjoint events have union probability $P(A)+P(B)$.

problems.title: Maximum term index
problems.question: Find the index of the largest term aₙ=−2n²+⌊20.26⌋n−19.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: $\lfloor20.26\rfloor=20$ and $a_n=31-2(n-5)^2$.
steps: The square is smallest at natural index n=5.

problems.title: Perpendicular lines
problems.question: Find the cosine of the angle between x+2y=1 and 2x−y=2.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: The slopes are −1/2 and 2, their product −1.
steps: The lines are perpendicular and cos 90°=0.

problems.title: Two hexagon-associated circle areas
problems.question: Find the ratio of the incircle are a to the circumcircle are a of a regular hexagon.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
steps: Square this radius ratio to get the disk-are a ratio.

problems.title: Which sequence is not decreasing?
problems.question: Which is not decreasing: $a_n=1/n-n$, $b_n=(2n+1)/(n+1)$, $c_n=-n^2-9n+10$?
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
steps: The reciprocal subtracted in bₙ decreases with n, so bₙ increases. The other two strictly decrease.

problems.title: Positive sequence terms
problems.question: How many positive terms has aₙ=80/(n+2)−n for natural n≥1?
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: The denominator is positive, so positivity means $80>n(n+2)$, or $(n+1)^2<81$.
steps: Thus n<8 and the valid indices are 1,…,7.

problems.title: Inverse of a rational function
problems.question: Find the inverse of $f(x)=1-1/(x+1)$.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: The equation is $y=x/(x+1)$. Solve $y(x+1)=x$.
steps: Then x(1−y)=y, so x=y/(1−y). Swap the variables. The inverse domain excludes 1.

problems.title: Arithmetic progression of angles
problems.question: Triangle angles for m an arithmetic progression and its middle-length side is 9. Find circumcircle are a.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: The middle angle is $180°/3=60°$. The side opposite it is the middle-length side.
steps: By the extended sine rule, R=9/(2sin60°)=3√3. Thus disk are a=π·27.

problems.title: Sector angle from arc and area
problems.question: A sector has arc length 4 and are a 8. Find its angle in radians.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: $S=rl/2$ and $\theta=l/r$.
steps: 8=r·4/2 gives r=4. Thus θ=4/4.

problems.title: A statistical condition determines x
problems.question: Data are x,1,2,0,4,3. Their mean equals the average of their median and unique mode. Find x.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: A unique mode requires $x\in\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, since otherwise all six observations are distinct. The mean is $(10+x)/6$.
steps: For x=0,1,2,3,4, the medians are 1.5,1.5,2,2.5,2.5, respectively. Their averages with mode x are.75,1.25,2,2.75,3.25. Compare with the means 10/6,11/6,2,13/6,14/6: only x=2 agrees.

problems.title: An even-length geometric progression
problems.question: An even-length geometric progression has total sum 3 times the sum of its odd-index terms. First term 6, last 192. Find its term count.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: Pair consecutive odd/even terms. Each pair is $(b_{2j-1},qb_{2j-1})$, so $S=(1+q)S_{odd}$.
steps: Here the odd sum is nonzero: with first term 6, it is 6(1+q²+…)>0. Thus 1+q=3, giving q=2. The last term condition 6·2^(N−1)=192 yields 2^(N−1)=32=2⁵.

problems.title: Three equal-sized arithmetic blocks
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has S₄=30, S₈=100. Find S₁₂.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: The sums of consecutive blocks of 4 terms themselves for m an arithmetic progression.
steps: Block 1 sums to 30, block 2 to 100−30=70. Their difference is 40, so block 3 sums to 110. Add 30+70+110.

problems.title: Alternate side midpoints of a regular hexagon
problems.question: A regular hexagon has side $4\sqrt[4]3$. Join the midpoints of every other side. Find the resulting triangle are a.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: The three selected midpoints for m an equilateral triangle with circumradius equal to the hexagon apothem $r=a\sqrt3/2$. Its are a is $(3\sqrt3/4)r^2$.

problems.title: An altitude from coordinate area
problems.question: A=(−2,−2), B=(1,−1), C=(2,1). Find the altitude from B to AC.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: $AC=(4,3)$ has length 5, and $AB=(3,1)$. The determinant magnitude is $|4\cdot1-3\cdot3|=5$.
steps: The determinant equals AC times the altitude from B, so h=5/5.

problems.title: A six-term recurrence cycle
problems.question: b₁=5, b₂=2, bₙ₊₂=bₙ₊₁−bₙ. Find b₂₀₂₆.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: The terms are 5,2,−3,−5,−2,3,5,2,… . The pair(5,2) repeats, so the deterministic recurrence has period 6.
steps: 2026≡4 mod 6. Therefore b₂₀₂₆=b₄.

problems.title: A power modulo seven
problems.question: A digit x satisfies 4¹⁹⁹≡x mod 7. Find x.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: $4^1\equiv4$, $4^2\equiv2$, $4^3\equiv1\pmod7$.
steps: The power cycle has length 3, and 199≡1 mod 3. Thus the residue is 4. Among decimal digits only 4 is congruent to 4 modulo 7.

problems.title: A sum of real cube roots
problems.question: Evaluate $\sqrt[3]{2+\sqrt5}+\sqrt[3]{2-\sqrt5}$.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: Let the roots be u, v. Then $u^3+v^3=4$ and $uv=\sqrt[3]{-1}=-1$.
steps: Their sum s satisfies s³=4−3s, or s³+3s−4=0. Factor(s−1)(s²+s+4)=0. The quadratic discriminant is −15, so the only real root is 1.

problems.title: Vectors from a centroid
problems.question: A=(0,4), B=(4,0), C=(−1,−1), and O is the centroid. Find cos of the angle between OA and OB.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
steps: OA=(−1,3), OB=(3,−1). Their dot product is −6 and both lengths√10. Thus cosθ=−6/10.

problems.title: Two parallel tangents to a circle
problems.question: Line y=kx+b is tangent to x²+y²−2x+4y+3=0 and perpendicular to x−y=1. Find |k−b|.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: The circle has centre(1,−2), radius √2. Perpendicularity gives k=−1. Its tangent equation is x+y−b=0.
steps: The centre distance must be √2:|1−2−b|/√2=√2. Thus|b+1|=2, so b=1 or −3. For either,|k−b|=|−1−b|=2.

problems.title: Three selected arithmetic terms form a geometric progression
problems.question: An increasing arithmetic progression starts at 2. Its 2nd,7th,27th terms for m a geometric progression. Find its difference.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: The condition is $(2+6d)^2=(2+d)(2+26d)$, with d>0.
steps: Expand to get 4+24d+36d²=4+54d+26d². Thus 10d(d−3)=0. Positivity excludes 0.

problems.title: Minimum under a sum constraint
problems.question: Distinct positive a, b satisfy a²−12a=b²−12b. Minimise a²+2b².
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: Factoring gives $(a-b)(a+b-12)=0$. Distinctness forces a+b=12.
steps: Substitute a=12−b: a²+2b²=3b²−24b+144=3(b−4)²+96. Equality at b=4, a=8 satisfies positivity and distinctness.

problems.title: A quadratic solution interval inside another interval
problems.question: Choose a uniformly from[−12,12]. Find the probability that ax²−2(a−1)x+a−1≥0 has a nonempty solution set entirely inside x²−2x≤0.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: The target interval is $[0,2]$. For a≥0 the first inequality has unbounded solutions, so it cannot qualify. For a<0 its discriminant is $4(1-a)>0$, so its solution set is a nonempty bounded interval.
steps: For a<0, the vertex x=1−1/a is positive and f(0)=a−1<0, so both roots are positive. Requiring the upper root≤2 is equivalent to having the vertex≤2 and f(2)=a+3≤0. These conditions reduce to a≤−3.
Inside[−12,12], the favourable interval is[−12,−3], length 9, out of total 24.

problems.title: Area of a semicircle slice
problems.question: AB is a semicircle diameter. C lies on AB, CD⊥AB and D lies on the arc. AC=$2+\sqrt2$, CB=$2-\sqrt2$. Find are a bounded by BC, CD and arc BD.
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: $AB=4,R=2$. With O the centre, $OC=\sqrt2$ and $CD=\sqrt{AC\cdot CB}=\sqrt2$. Hence angle BOD=45°.
steps: The requested region is sector BOD minus right triangle OCD. Sector are a=(45/360)π·4=π/2. Triangle are a=(1/2)√2·√2=1.

problems.title: Orthogonality with prescribed vector lengths
problems.question: |b|=2|a|. Which listed k allows(a+b)·(4a−kb)=0?
problems.idea: Use exact algebra, counting, or the appropriate geometric formula.
formulas: Assume |a|>0 and put $a\cdot b=2|a|^2\cos\theta$. The condition becomes $4-4k+2(4-k)\cos\theta=0$.
steps: For k≠4, this gives cosθ=2(k−1)/(4−k). A real angle requires 4(k−1)²≤(4−k)², or k²≤4. Among the listed choices only k=2 qualifies. At k=2, cosθ=1, so b=2a and 4a−kb=0.
problems.note: This choice makes the second vector zero. If “perpendicular” requires two nonzero vectors with an actual 90° angle, none of the listed choices works. Under the dot-product definition, the zero vector is orthogonal to every vector.
